The EU Delegation in Nairobi represents the European Union in Kenya, working in close coordination with the Embassies of the EU Member States. Additionally, it hosts the Regional Partnerships Unit which manages EU external cooperation programs and investments in Eastern Africa. Offer We offer a position as a “Finance and Contracts Officer” within the Regional Partnerships Unit at the EU Delegation to Kenya. Successful candidate will join the Global Gateway team covering education, health, agriculture and food security. The workplace is Nairobi, for a fixed term contract of two (2) years, with possible extension/renewal, subject to six months’ probation and it is open to Kenya nationals and residents with a valid work permit. We offer a competitive position in a lively and multicultural environment. Full time of 37.5 hours per week (under flexible time regime) and remunerated according to a salary table in shillings (basic minimum 511,049KES), including a supplementary pension scheme and medical insurance, offered to employees and their families under certain conditions. After recruitment, the chosen candidate will occupy a specific Local Agent job Category 1, for a job description that can evolve according to the needs. The role supports the Team Leader and advises colleagues on issues within the scope of the financial initiator function. Liaise with other staff members in the section, as needed, and provide advice and comments on draft financing agreements, identification and action fiches as well as on financial and budgetary matters. Take part in negotiations of technical and financial aspects of contracts linked to the preparation and implementation of external projects. Provide advice on financial and budgetary matters to the staff in the section of the Delegation, with a high degree of autonomy. Provide and organise training on contractual and financial matters for Delegation staff and beneficiaries. Independently monitor and manage the performance, priorities, and progress of the operations under her/his responsibility, and promptly bring any significant problems, together with proposed solutions, to the Team Leader’s attention. Ensure proper archiving and filing of documents related to EU external programmes. Contribute to the preparation of reports for Delegation and Commission management and in providing support to visiting missions. BUDGET and FINANCE Ensure financial initiation. Check financial aspects of contracts, draft documents linked to financial operations (addenda, payment orders, recovery orders, debit notes). Ensure that the adequate financial circuits are in place and followed. Advise and comment on draft financing agreements, identification and action fiches. Provide advice on sound financial management and application of EU rules. Ensure the quality (including accuracy and comprehensiveness) of the data entered into specific informatic tools. Contribute to the reporting requirements and interface with EU HQ financial services when necessary. Responsible for the proper functioning of informatics tools for budgetary and accountancy management and coherence of data between different databases. Contribute to the preparation and negotiations of technical and financial aspects of contracts. Ensure the financial initiation of new contracts, amendments and closures in line with internal rules and procedures. Ensure the accurate encoding and financial initiation of payments, clearings, recovery orders, in line with internal rules and procedures. AUDIT, CONTROL and INSPECTION Ensure an adequate follow-up of recommendations issued by the control bodies and auditors. Contribute to the preparation of financial reports and statistics follow-up of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and other performance indicators. Assist in the drafting of the Annual Audit Plan. review_candidates.title: Deputy Chief Financial Officer
review_candidates.description: About Community Housing Canberra (CHC) Australia CHC Australia is the largest not-for-profit provider of affordable and social housing based in Canberra, and the region's only Tier 1 registered community housing provider. Over more than 25 years it has grown to house over 2,000 Canberrans, with a team of 45 staff. CHC is unusual in its sector. It both develops and manages properties, using its own development activity to help fund new supply and the services that sit alongside it, in addition to government funding. The model is working well, but CHC is now preparing to scale it significantly beyond anything it has done before. In June 2026, the ACT Government announced a significant new investment in housing, expected to support around $650 million in community housing projects and help unlock new affordable homes through the Commonwealth’s Housing Australia Future Fund. CHC is positioning itself to play a significant role in that growth. It has a pipeline of more than 1,000 new homes and over the next three years expects to grow its portfolio to around 2,400 properties through a mix of new development, turnkey purchases and acquisitions. The Opportunity Growth at this scale isn’t linear. Each acquisition sits within its own special purpose vehicle, with its own board, governance and reporting requirements. That means CHC’s corporate capability can’t simply keep pace with portfolio growth, it needs to be built ahead of it. That’s the opportunity for the newly created Deputy Chief Financial Officer. Working alongside the CFO, you’ll strengthen the finance capability, systems and operating discipline CHC needs for its next stage of growth and play an active role in the strategy around investment, feasibility, systems and how CHC scales. A change program is already mapping the processes and systems CHC will need, including a move from its current finance system to purpose-built software. You’ll help shape those decisions and lead the work through implementation, rather than inheriting a model that has already been built. Strengthen the finance function for an organisation preparing to grow its portfolio by around two-thirds Take day-to-day ownership of FP&A, transactional finance, tax and asset operations Lead feasibility modelling and scenario analysis to support investment decisions and enable CHC to take on more projects Shape and deliver a major finance system replacement, moving from legacy software to a purpose-built community housing platform Work directly with the Board, committees and executive from the outset, stepping in for the CFO when required Lead three direct reports and a wider team of around 10 across finance, asset management and IT The Role You’ll partner with the CFO across CHC’s finance, asset and systems portfolio, with direct ownership of the areas that need to scale fastest. CHC is at the beginning of a significant transformation, and you’ll be joining while the systems, processes and structures are still evolving. You’ll need to be comfortable with ambiguity, good at bringing order to complexity and willing to roll up your sleeves when needed. You’ll also need the patience and resilience to stay focused on the longer-term outcome and enjoy seeing the pieces come together over time. You’ll bring a commercial mindset to a for-purpose environment. There is strong capability in the existing team; your role is to strengthen the structure around them. review_candidates.title: Chief Operating Officer & Secretary General
review_candidates.description: ABOUT BLUEMIND FOUNDATION Mental health is health. Bluemind Foundation is a non profit organization with a clear mission: make mental health care accessible to everyone, everywhere, every day. THE MANDATE The Chief Operating Officer & Secretary General is Bluemind Foundation's senior executive responsible for institutional execution. The COO translates strategy into results, leads day-to-day organizational management, strengthens the Leadership Team and builds the systems required for scale. The COO ensures that commitments made to communities, governments, partners, funders and the Board are delivered on time. The COO serves as the President's principal executive partner and creates the operating conditions that allow the President to focus on vision, resource mobilization, government engagement, strategic partnerships and external leadership. As Secretary General, the COO ensures effective governance, Board processes, institutional accountability and execution of Board decisions. This is an institution-building mandate requiring judgment, ownership, management discipline and a high tolerance for complexity. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Strategy Execution & Organizational Performance • Translate strategic priorities into annual and quarterly plans with clear outcomes, owners, budgets and milestones. • Establish a disciplined operating rhythm, including leadership meetings, dashboards, decision tracking and accountability mechanisms. • Ensure reliable and timely execution across programmes and institutional functions. • Identify bottlenecks, risks and performance gaps early and drive their resolution. • Build management systems capable of supporting national-scale implementation and regional growth. • Keep organizational priorities focused, adequately resourced and aligned with the Foundation's mission. 2. Executive Leadership & People • Lead and strengthen the Leadership Team. • Clarify roles, decision rights, responsibilities and performance expectations. Recruit, develop and retain exceptional talent.• Build a culture of excellence, accountability, collaboration, learning and care. • Develop leadership capacity through coaching, feedback and effective performance management. • Build teams capable of owning execution without routine escalation to the President. 3. Finance, Operations, Risk & Compliance • With the CFO, oversee financial planning, budgeting, cash-flow management, controls and institutional reporting. • Strengthen HR, procurement, legal, administrative and operational systems. • Maintain rigorous donor compliance and stewardship. • Lead foundation risk management and timely escalation of material risks. • Ensure full compliance with applicable laws, agreements and organizational policies. • Maintain very high standards of safeguarding, ethics, transparency and accountability. 4. Governance & Executive Office • Serve as Secretary General to the Board of Directors. • Coordinate Board meetings, documentation, resolutions and follow-through. • Ensure timely execution of Board decisions. • Provide the President and Board with clear dashboards, executive reports and decision-ready information. • Advise the President on organizational performance, people, risk, execution and institutional priorities. • Maintain clear governance boundaries and effective coordination between the Board, President and management. 5. Government, Partnerships & Resource Mobilization • Ensure Bluemind Foundation has the institutional capacity required to deliver alongside governments at national scale. • Partner with the President on resource mobilization, translating priorities into strong pipelines, proposals, budgets, stewardship and follow-through. • Oversee major institutional proposals, agreements and donor commitments. Mental health is health. www.bluemindfoundation.org • Represent Bluemind Foundation externally when delegated by the President. • Ensure new partnerships and expansion opportunities are operationally and financially sound. WHY JOIN BLUEMIND FOUNDATION? Bluemind Foundation is moving from breakthrough innovation to an institution capable of delivering excellence repeatedly, reliably and at scale. We call this Care Starts With Us: building inside the Foundation the same high standards of care, trust, accountability and excellence we want to see in the systems we help transform. As COO & Secretary General, you will help build that institution alongside the President, Board and team. WHO WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE As a dream executor, you are an exceptional operator and institution-builder who has already carried significant organizational responsibility and knows how to turn ambition into reliable execution. You have built, scaled or transformed something complex. You can point to teams, systems or institutions that became measurably stronger because you were there. You are a leader of leaders. You set clear expectations, hold people accountable and develop strong teams. You can challenge a Board member or senior colleague constructively, and you are secure enough to lead alongside a highly visible and entrepreneurial founder. You understand that trust is earned through reliability. When you make a commitment, people know it will be delivered. You bring strong financial and operational judgment and can engage credibly with governments, institutional funders, Boards and international partners. You can move comfortably between a leadership meeting, a government discussion and the operational realities of teams delivering on the ground. We expect you to bring: • 10+ years of senior leadership experience, including substantial responsibility for teams, budgets and organizational performance. • A demonstrated record of building, scaling or transforming organizations, programmes or complex operating systems, with results you can evidence. • Experience leading teams and creating clear accountability across functions. Mental health is health. www.bluemindfoundation.org • Strong command of financial management, organizational planning, operations, risk and performance management. • Experience working with governments, institutional funders, Boards and complex partnerships, ideally across African and international environments. • Strong judgment under pressure and the ability to make decisions with incomplete information. • Full professional fluency in French and English, written and spoken. • High integrity, intellectual curiosity, humility, loyalty and personal accountability. Experience in Francophone Africa is highly desirable. Experience in public health, international development, philanthropy, government or another mission-driven environment is valuable. We care more about evidence that you can do this work than about having followed one particular career path. We value leaders who combine low ego with high standards; kindness and excellence; strategic range with operational depth; ambition with discipline; and confidence with the ability to listen. THE LEADERSHIP PARTNERSHIP The President and COO & Secretary General operate as a close executive partnership with clear accountability and decision rights. The President holds the Foundation's vision, strategic direction, high-level government and external relationships, resource mobilization leadership and public voice. The COO owns institutional execution and ensures that the people, systems and resources required to deliver that vision perform at the level Bluemind's next chapter demands. The standard is simple enough: commitments become execution, execution becomes results, and the institution becomes stronger with every stage of growth. HOW TO APPLY Please send your CV and application to welcome@bluemindfoundation.org, with the subject line: COO & Secretary General – Your Name No traditional cover letter is required. Instead, please answer the following three questions in no more than 200 words each: 1. Why you, why Bluemind, why now? Why does Bluemind Foundation's mission and this particular institution-building challenge make sense for the next chapter of your career? 2. What have you built or changed that best demonstrates your fit for this role? Tell us about one professional accomplishment you are most proud of and that best demonstrates your ability to succeed in this role. What was the situation, what did you personally own, what did you change or build, and what measurable result followed? 3. What would you build first? You join Bluemind Foundation at a moment of strong momentum and increasing complexity, with too much execution still dependent on its founder. Based on this job description, what would your three priorities be during your first six months, and why? Please also include: • Three professional references who have worked directly with you, ideally including a former manager, a peer and someone you have managed. Please indicate their role, organization, relationship to you and contact details. References will be with your knowledge. • Any former manager or employer you would prefer us not to contact, and why. This will not count against your application. We value context, transparency, candour and accountability. • Your salary expectations. We operate with the financial discipline of a nonprofit organization, but budget will not be the reason we walk away from an exceptional fit. We prefer an open conversation about what is possible. • Your earliest possible starting date. The appointment will begin with a six-month consultancy period, giving both the successful candidate and Bluemind Foundation the opportunity to test the partnership in practice. Subject to successful completion and mutual agreement, the position will transition into a long-term executive appointment.

review_candidates.description: Rejoignez MIGEN MIGEN est un acteur majeur de la prestation de maintenance industrielle, en forte croissance et dirigé par des hommes et des femmes de terrain. Nous accompagnons nos clients industriels grâce à des équipes techniques spécialisées, principalement dans les métiers de la maintenance industrielle, de l’électromécanique, de l’automatisme et de la robotique. Dans le cadre du développement ponctuel de nos activités, nous ouvrons exceptionnellement un poste de Chargé de travaux électriques spécialisé en travaux sous tension basse tension (B2T) . Ce poste vient compléter notre expertise terrain et répond à des besoins spécifiques de nos clients en matière de travaux, de modification, de dépannage et d'interventions électriques en basse tension. Rejoindre MIGEN, c’est intégrer une entreprise à taille humaine, proche du terrain, où la sécurité, l’expertise technique et la qualité des interventions sont au cœur de notre fonctionnement. Vous habitez à Rezé ou à proximité ? Ce poste est basé à Rezé et les interventions se concentrent sur le secteur. Vos missions Vous intervenez chez nos clients industriels et tertiaires pour des travaux neufs, des modifications d'installation et du dépannage en basse tension. En tant que Chargé de travaux , vous êtes responsable de la préparation, de l'organisation et de la sécurité des interventions, de l'analyse des risques jusqu'à la remise de l'ouvrage. Préparation et sécurité Prendre connaissance de l'ouvrage et des contraintes du site et réaliser les visites préalables avec le client. Réaliser les analyses de risques et définir les modes opératoires. Définir la zone de travail et le balisage. Déterminer les conditions d'exécution du travail (CET) applicables aux opérations sous tension et en vérifier la faisabilité. Recevoir l'attestation de consignation ou l'autorisation de travail. Assurer la relation avec le chargé d'exploitation électrique du site. Contrôler l'adéquation, la validité et l'état du matériel, de l'outillage isolé, des VAT, EPI et EPC. Conduite des travaux Donner les consignes de sécurité aux exécutants, répartir les tâches et surveiller en permanence leur réalisation. Réaliser les interventions électriques : raccordements, reprises de départs, remplacement d'appareillage, câblage d'armoires et de TGBT, distribution, éclairage et alimentation de machines. Diagnostiquer et dépanner les installations BT, y compris en régime dégradé et sous contrainte de production. Réaliser les mesures, essais et contrôles avant remise en service. Procéder à la remise de l'ouvrage au client. Suivi et relation client Rédiger les comptes rendus d'intervention, relevés et rapports de mesure. Mettre à jour les schémas et le DOE. Assurer l'interface technique quotidienne avec le client. Identifier et remonter les éventuels besoins complémentaires au service coordination. Participer à la démarche QHSE : port des EPI, remontée des situations dangereuses et quarts d'heure sécurité. Votre profil Vous êtes issu(e) d'une formation Bac Pro MELEC, BTS Électrotechnique, BTS Maintenance des Systèmes ou disposez d'une expérience équivalente. Vous justifiez d'au moins 5 ans d'expérience en électricité industrielle ou tertiaire , avec une pratique confirmée des travaux sous tension BT . Vous disposez de l'habilitation B2T . Vous maîtrisez : La lecture et l'interprétation des schémas électriques. Les régimes de neutre, l'appareillage BT et les dispositifs de protection. Les opérations de dépannage et d'intervention sur installations électriques BT. La préparation et l'organisation de travaux électriques. L'encadrement d'une petite équipe. Vous êtes reconnu(e) pour votre rigueur, votre sens des responsabilités et votre capacité à garder votre sang-froid face aux aléas . Votre sens du service client, votre pédagogie et votre aisance rédactionnelle seront également importants dans ce poste. Prérequis Habilitation B2T en cours de validité selon la norme NF C 18-510. Formation TST BT à jour, avec recyclage de moins de 3 ans. Permis B indispensable. Aptitude médicale compatible avec les travaux sous tension et le travail en hauteur. Les habilitations B2V, BR, BC, H0V , ainsi que le CACES R486 catégorie B, l'AIPR et le SST sont appréciés. Les formations nécessaires peuvent être complétées ou financées à l'embauche. Rémunération et avantages 34 000 à 40 000 € brut annuels, sur 12 mois, selon votre expérience, vos habilitations et votre niveau d'autonomie. Paniers repas. Indemnités de déplacement selon la grille en vigueur. Astreintes et interventions ponctuelles le week-end rémunérées. Mutuelle d'entreprise et prévoyance. Camion nacelle mis à disposition de l'équipe. Téléphone, tablette et outillage individuel fournis. Intégration accompagnée par le service coordination et binôme lors des premières interventions. Poste basé à Nantes (44), avec déplacements quotidiens sur un rayon d'environ 60 km.
